facts: The paper asks whether it is possible to use out-of-domain acoustic training data to improve a speech recognizer's performance on a specific, independent application.
The experiments use Wallstreet Journal (WSJ) data to train a recognizer.
The trained recognizer is adapted in the Phonebook domain.
The trained recognizer is evaluated in the Phonebook domain.
The Wallstreet Journal and Phonebook corpora share US English as a common language.
The Wallstreet Journal and Phonebook corpora differ in many important respects.
The Wallstreet Journal and Phonebook corpora differ in microphone versus telephone channel.
The Wallstreet Journal and Phonebook corpora differ in continuous speech versus isolated words.
There is a mismatch in speaking rate between the Wallstreet Journal and Phonebook corpora.
The paper deals with two questions.
One question asks how much adaptation data from the Phonebook training corpus is necessary to achieve a reasonable recognition performance starting from the WSJ-trained recognizer.
The adaptation data are taken from the Phonebook training corpus.
There is a high degree of mismatch.
A second question asks whether additional out-of-domain training data can improve the recognition performance of a Phonebook-trained baseline acoustic model.
The paper describes adaptation and normalization techniques used to bridge the mismatch between the two corpora.
